text:
deploy-bot: Initiating CONFIG-ONLY rollout cfg-20260321-01 for change window 2026-03-21T02:00Z->2026-03-21T04:00Z. Canary target: 5% traffic to canary pool (gpu-canary-1). Changes: routing weights, request timeouts, batching window, per-route token caps. Rollout plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%, 10m wait + health checks between steps. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/config-rollouts/cfg-20260321-01
sarah: Quick question — are we pinning model variants for the canary? Last time routing+timeout mismatch triggered model fallback and skewed metrics.
matt: yes, pinning recommended. Plan: canary -> model: rwd-model-v2.1-canary, stable -> rwd-model-v2.0. Command I ran locally:
```
redwoodctl pin --route "/v1/fast" --model rwd-model-v2.1-canary --config cfg-20260321-01
```
raj: Noted. Also increase batching window slightly to absorb short spikes. Proposed change: batching.window_ms 8 -> 15. That should lower per-token cost but might add ~6-10ms p99.
emily: Timeout change? Docs say we're lowering per-request timeout from 20s -> 12s for faster failover. Is that safe for long hallucination jobs?
oliver: For long-run jobs we have separate /v1/long route untouched. This change is only for latency-sensitive routes: /v1/fast and /v1/generate. Also setting per-route token_cap: /v1/fast = 2048 -> 4096, /v1/generate stays 8192.
matt: Adding routing tweak: move 5% weight from /v1/generate -> /v1/fast to favor fast path under typical traffic shape. YAML diff in config:
```
routes:
  /v1/fast:
    weight: 15  # was 10
    model: rwd-model-v2.1-canary  # pinned for canary subset
  /v1/generate:
    weight: 85  # was 90
```
sarah: Monitoring hooks? We need 429/504/timeout alarms and a regression detector on mean latency for canary vs baseline.
deploy-bot: Watchers set: @sre-oncall, @prod-observability. Alerts: canary_5m_error_rate>1% or canary_p95_latency_change>20% will pause rollout automatically.
raj: Let's also enable per-route QPS shaper on /v1/fast: peak qps cap 1200 -> 800 for first two steps to avoid saturating small canary pool.
emily: Suggest adding rollback criteria to the thread so oncall knows steps.
matt: Draft rollback steps:
1) pause rollout (automated by deploy-bot on alert)
2) revert to previous config cfg-20260318-stable via `redwoodctl apply --config cfg-20260318-stable`
3) pin routes back to rwd-model-v2.0 if model fallback observed
4) open incident channel #inc-urgent if >10% user impact for >15m
sarah: +1. Also add a soft hold at 20% for manual check of logs and cost deltas.
deploy-bot: Rollout step 1 -> set canary 5%. Starting now. Start timestamp: 1891234567.
deploy-bot: Canary applied to pool gpu-canary-1. Health checks: OK (3/3). Waiting 10m for metrics.
(8m later)
raj: Seeing small uptick in 429s for /v1/fast on the canary pool, from 0.1% -> 0.6% but still under alert. Acceptable? Can we throttle more aggressively for canary? Should we pause expansion to 20%?
emily: I'm seeing p95 latency +12% for canary vs baseline in last 5m. Not huge but combined with 429 uptick I'd prefer to hold at 5% until we confirm batching/window effect.
matt: Agreed. Hold at 5%. I'll annotate the rollout ticket with current metrics and decision: HOLD -> investigate batching window interaction with cache TTL.
sarah: Investigation note: KV cache TTL was bumped from 30s -> 90s in this config to improve reuse. That could change latency distribution for cold starts. Check cache hit-rate on canary.
oliver: Cache hit-rate on canary: 62% vs 59% baseline. So caching improved, but latency bump likely due to increased batching.window_ms causing higher scheduling latency for p95. Try lowering batching to 12ms in the canary config only.
matt: If we adjust canary config, we need a config patch rather than full rollback. Propose cfg-20260321-01a with batching.window_ms=12 for canary pool only.
raj: I can cut the patch. Command:
```
redwoodctl patch --config cfg-20260321-01 --set "pools[gpu-canary-1].batching.window_ms=12" --out cfg-20260321-01a
redwoodctl apply --config cfg-20260321-01a
```
matt: Apply when ready and re-run health checks for 10m. Keep hold at 5% until metrics stable.
deploy-bot: Patch applied as cfg-20260321-01a. Canary now running with updated batching parameters. Health checks: 2/3 passed (collector lagging). Waiting 10m.
(9m later)
emily: Post-patch: canary p95 now +4% vs baseline, 429s back to 0.12%. Looks safe to proceed to 20% but keep throttles: qps cap 800 for canary for next step.
sarah: OK to advance to 20% after a manual thumbs-up from @sre-oncall.
raj: @sre-oncall please chime in.
oliver: @sre-oncall gave verbal ok (DM). Advancing to 20%.
deploy-bot: Rolling to 20% now. Expected completion in ~30s.
deploy-bot: Rollout reached 20%. Health: OK. Monitoring will auto-pause on alerts.
matt: I'll prepare release notes snippet:
"Config-only release cfg-20260321-01a: adjusted routing weights (shifted 5% to /v1/fast), increased per-route token cap for /v1/fast to 4096, tightened request timeout on latency-sensitive routes to 12s, adjusted batching window to 12ms for canary, added qps shaper for canary pool. Pinned canary to rwd-model-v2.1-canary. Rollout staged with automated pause on errors."
sarah: I'll push that to the changelog and GA release notes.
emily: Add cost note: expect slight token cost decrease from batching improvements but watch GPU utilization as we raise to 50%.
raj: Closing loop: if any of the automated alerts fire, rollout will pause and follow the rollback steps. If stable at 50% for 1h, we proceed to 100%.
matt: nice work. tagging this thread into the release ticket.
deploy-bot: Rollout status: 20% complete, cfg-20260321-01a, last update 1891234620. If you need to force rollback: `redwoodctl rollback --config cfg-20260321-01a --to cfg-20260318-stable`
